name: Deception: Murder in Hong Kong
summary: Social deduction murder mystery where a forensic scientist gives tile clues while the hidden murderer among investigators tries to mislead.
rules_text: Players get secret roles: 1 Forensic Scientist, 1 Murderer, optional Accomplice and Witness, rest Investigators. Each non-scientist has 4 Clue and 4 Means cards displayed outward. Secretly, with eyes closed, Murderer points to one of their own Clue as Key Evidence and one Means as Means of Murder; Accomplice and Witness learn identities via the Scientist. Then for three rounds Scientist reveals 6 Scene tiles and places bullet markers on one item per tile as clues to the solution, possibly replacing one tile each round after the first. Between markers players discuss publicly and in turn present their guess for 30 seconds. Any player may spend their badge to attempt to solve by naming one Clue and one Means on the table. If correct, Investigators and Scientist win, unless Witness rule triggers: if Murderer was identified but then correctly names Witness, Murderer side wins. Otherwise after third presentation if never solved correctly, Murderer side wins.
rating_reason: Social deduction hidden murderer clue game fits hidden roles.
